title: Choose the home screen
question: Three compositions of the same canon world for the Home surface at 412×915. Same palette, same type, same facts in all three. Pick the one that should become the build's first viewport.

options.label: The Summary
options.thesis: The month total owns the top of the screen at 42px, a donut carries the category split, and six recent rows sit in a soft white card. The category convention, drawn correctly: the number first, the detail beneath, one floating add pill.
materials: soft white card of recent rows
options.viewport: Big number, donut, chips, six rows, one pill. The calmest of the three and the least dense — the month's shape is legible before any single expense is.
options.risk: The donut is a second reading of the same four numbers the legend already lists, and only six rows fit, so the ledger the app exists to keep is mostly below the fold.

options.label: Capture First
options.lineage: capture-led home with a stacked split bar
options.thesis: The bordered ask field is the largest element on the screen — Bengali prompt, two keys, camera in blue — so the first thing the eye lands on is the thing you type into. The month becomes a compact card under it with a nine-pixel stacked bar doing the work the donut did.
materials: bordered ask field with Bengali ghost prompt
muted mic key and blue camera key
options.viewport: Ask field, month card with split bar and inline legend, one chip row, then day-grouped rows under a fixed bottom nav. Capture, then the month, then the days.
options.risk: The month totals sit below the capture field, so a user opening the app to check a number reads the ask prompt first. Bottom nav costs 66px of an 915px screen.

options.label: Ledger First
options.lineage: dense day-grouped ledger with inline chip amounts
options.thesis: Everything above the rows is compressed into one header block so the ledger starts high and runs edge to edge. Category chips carry their amounts inline instead of in a legend, and eight-pixel colour squares replace icon tiles to buy density.
options.viewport: Header, amber sync strip, five day groups with subtotals, ten rows, FAB. The most expenses visible at once and the only composition that shows the offline state in the first viewport.
options.risk: The busiest screen. Colour squares carry category by hue alone with no glyph, and the amber strip takes prime space whether or not the user is offline.
